sections.title: Reclining sphinxes and no visible reins
sections.bodyMarkdown:
An armoured figure stands in the chariot beneath a star-shaped crown ornament and a blue canopy patterned with stars. Crescent-shaped decorations with faces sit on his shoulders; a square appears on his chest, and small symbols line the panels below his belt. On the left of the picture, he holds a staff, while his other hand rests at the edge of the vehicle.

One black and one white sphinx recline side by side before the chariot, their heads and bodies not oriented in exactly the same way. The vehicle bears a winged circular design and a shield-shaped ornament. Walls, towers, and a band of water are visible behind. The figure looks firmly positioned, but there is no running, spinning wheel, or cloud of dust to justify describing a high-speed charge.

[View the RWS image examined for this article](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_07_Chariot.jpg)

sections.title: Reaching a goal is not understanding everything
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Waite associates the Chariot with conquest and victory, particularly achievements of the mind and the outer world. He also cautions that such achievements do not mean the figure has attained inner spiritual understanding. That limitation matters: reaching one goal does not resolve every question.

The text also describes the object in the figure’s hand as a drawn sword, whereas a staff is visible in the colour RWS image examined here. Our image description follows the artwork and preserves this discrepancy, rather than treating every sentence in the book as an exact inventory of the picture.

[Read Waite’s original English discussion](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar07.htm)

sections.title: Reading it reversed
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Here, the reversal suggests a problem with how progress is being pursued. People may be aiming at different goals, speed may exceed preparation, or the insistence that “I must win” may obscure the actual cost. Visible busyness does not always bring you closer to the intended destination.

Slow down and check before applying more force. Examine the purpose, resources, and division of work separately, and identify two demands that conflict. If the goal itself no longer fits, choosing another direction is also an exercise of control.

sections.title: Everyday examples

### A project approaches delivery

Define the essential result for this delivery and defer new requests that would scatter the effort. Maintain coordination through checkable milestones, rather than only urging everyone to sprint.

### Preparing for a competition or exam

### Two people want to move something forward

First confirm that you share a destination, then discuss who will do what. If one wants to accelerate and the other needs preparation, discuss concrete conditions rather than argue about who is more committed.

articleMarkdown:
# The Chariot — Bring different forces into a shared direction

VII · The Chariot · Major Arcana · RWS

**Keywords:** Direction · Coordination · Progress

**Upright at a glance:** Choose your direction, hold a steady pace, and keep moving.
**Reversed at a glance:** Effort is taking you off course. Recheck direction and coordination.

The Chariot looks commanding, but the two sphinxes in front are reclining, and no reins are drawn in the driver’s hands. What does it take to move a vehicle forward besides force?

## Reclining sphinxes and no visible reins

An armoured figure stands in the chariot beneath a star-shaped crown ornament and a blue canopy patterned with stars. Crescent-shaped decorations with faces sit on his shoulders; a square appears on his chest, and small symbols line the panels below his belt. On the left of the picture, he holds a staff, while his other hand rests at the edge of the vehicle.

One black and one white sphinx recline side by side before the chariot, their heads and bodies not oriented in exactly the same way. The vehicle bears a winged circular design and a shield-shaped ornament. Walls, towers, and a band of water are visible behind. The figure looks firmly positioned, but there is no running, spinning wheel, or cloud of dust to justify describing a high-speed charge.

[View the RWS image examined for this article](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_07_Chariot.jpg)

## Reaching a goal is not understanding everything

Waite associates the Chariot with conquest and victory, particularly achievements of the mind and the outer world. He also cautions that such achievements do not mean the figure has attained inner spiritual understanding. That limitation matters: reaching one goal does not resolve every question.

The text also describes the object in the figure’s hand as a drawn sword, whereas a staff is visible in the colour RWS image examined here. Our image description follows the artwork and preserves this discrepancy, rather than treating every sentence in the book as an exact inventory of the picture.

[Read Waite’s original English discussion](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar07.htm)

## Reading it upright

Upright, the card can help organize the direction and discipline a task requires. The motivation may already be present; now priorities, a steady rhythm, and competing needs must be brought into workable relation. The two sphinxes offer a visual prompt for this idea of coordination. That is this article’s learning association.

Once a goal is clear, you still need the ability to change route. Steady progress includes checking feedback, replenishing resources, and resting when necessary. Persistence means understanding why you are moving and which changes need a response, rather than never turning.

## Reading it reversed

Here, the reversal suggests a problem with how progress is being pursued. People may be aiming at different goals, speed may exceed preparation, or the insistence that “I must win” may obscure the actual cost. Visible busyness does not always bring you closer to the intended destination.

Slow down and check before applying more force. Examine the purpose, resources, and division of work separately, and identify two demands that conflict. If the goal itself no longer fits, choosing another direction is also an exercise of control.

## Everyday examples

### A project approaches delivery

Define the essential result for this delivery and defer new requests that would scatter the effort. Maintain coordination through checkable milestones, rather than only urging everyone to sprint.

### Preparing for a competition or exam

Schedule practice, review, and recovery together. Adjust intensity to what you are actually mastering; do not use uninterrupted hours of activity as proof of effort.

### Two people want to move something forward

First confirm that you share a destination, then discuss who will do what. If one wants to accelerate and the other needs preparation, discuss concrete conditions rather than argue about who is more committed.

## A short exercise

Draw two circles side by side and put one of the two most conflicting demands you face in each. Then write one shared goal for this week. Give each demand a place in the plan and remove one action unrelated to the goal.

## A common misreading

The Chariot does not guarantee a win, and its reversal cannot predict a traffic accident. It is more useful for checking direction, coordination, and cost. Actual safety and outcomes still depend on real-world judgment and action.

## Artwork and English-language sources

- [Pamela Colman Smith, The Chariot, RWS Pam-A](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_07_Chariot.jpg)
- [A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part II, VII. The Chariot (1911 transcription)](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar07.htm)
- [A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot, Part III §3, The Greater Arcana and Their Divinatory Meanings (1911 transcription)](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

Each image was individually inspected. The English source is the transcription labelled 1911; the artwork is the Pam-A scan identified on Commons. Sources checked: 2026-10-07.

The upright and reversed interpretations, examples, and exercises are original material for reflection, not line-by-line translations of old divinatory lists. Tarot cannot establish future events, another person’s thoughts, or a health condition.

sourceRecord.title: 战车 让不同的力量朝同一方向走
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 方向定了，把节奏稳住，继续往前推
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 使劲却走偏，先把方向和步调重新对齐
sourceRecord.hook: 战车看起来很有气势，车前的两只斯芬克斯却卧着，车手手中也没有画出缰绳。问题随之而来：让一辆车前进的，除了用力，还需要什么？
imageReading: 身穿护甲的人站在车中，头顶是星形冠饰与蓝色星纹顶篷。两肩有带面孔的月牙形装饰，胸前有方形图案，腰下的衣片排列着细小符号。他在画面左侧握着一根权杖，另一手靠在车沿。
车前一黑一白两只斯芬克斯并排卧着，头部与身体的朝向并不完全一致。车身中央画有带翅膀的圆形图案及盾形装饰，后方还能看到城墙、塔楼和水带。人物的位置很坚定，画面却没有呈现奔跑、车轮飞转或尘土，因此不能把它描述成正在高速冲锋。
tradition: Waite 将战车联系到征服与胜利，尤其强调心智和外在领域的成就；他同时提醒，这并不意味着人物已经获得内在的精神理解。这一限制很重要：赢得一个目标，不等于所有问题都解决了。
原文还把人物手中之物写成出鞘的剑，但本篇核对的 RWS 彩色图中可见的是权杖。图像描述按实际画面写，保留这个文本差异，不把原书每句话都当成对画面的精确记录。
uprightMeaning: 正位可以用来整理推进一件事所需的方向与纪律。你已经有动力，接下来要决定优先顺序、保持节奏，并让不同需求不再互相扯住。两只斯芬克斯可作为这种协调的视觉提示；这是本篇的学习联想。
明确目标之后，也要有调整路线的能力。稳定推进包括查看反馈、补充资源和必要的休息。坚持并不是从不转弯，而是知道为什么前进，以及哪些变化需要回应。
reversedMeaning: 本篇把逆位读作推进方式出了偏差：各方各有目标，速度超过了准备，或者为了保持“我必须赢”的姿态，忽略了实际代价。表面忙碌，也可能没有接近真正的目的地。
先减速核对，而不是一律加大力气。把目的、资源和分工分别看一遍，找出互相冲突的两项要求。若目标本身已不合适，重新选择方向也属于掌控。

situations.title: 项目进入交付阶段
situations.text: 确定这次必须交付的核心，暂缓会拉散方向的新增要求。用可检查的进度点保持协同，而不是只鼓励大家冲刺。

situations.title: 准备比赛或考试
situations.text: 把训练、复盘与恢复一起排进计划。看实际掌握程度调整强度，不用连续忙碌的时长证明努力。

situations.title: 两个人想一起推进一件事
situations.text: 先确认目的地是否相同，再谈谁做什么。若一方想加速、另一方需要准备，讨论具体条件比争论谁更积极更有用。

sourceRecord.practice: 画两个并列圆圈，分别写下眼前最拉扯你的两股需求，再写一个本周共同目标。为每股需求安排一个位置，删掉一项与目标无关的动作。
sourceRecord.commonMisread: 战车不会保证竞赛获胜，也不能根据逆位预言交通事故。它更适合帮助你检查方向、协调和代价；真正的安全与结果，仍要靠现实中的判断和行动。
sourceRecord.sourceClaim: 外在与心智领域的征服及其精神理解限制；两只斯芬克斯。原文sword与实际彩色画面权杖差异已明确。协调、纪律及逆位偏差为原创教学。
sourceRecord.readingApproach: 图像细读、Waite历史解释与原创现代反思分别标示；正逆位是学习与自我反思提示，不用来确认未来、健康或他人隐秘行为。
sourceRecord.reverseMethod: 当代反思式读法，依据正位主题的受阻、失衡或尚待整合展开；不是对Waite旧逆位词条逐项翻译。
